mainTopic: Who may receive מעשר ראשון, why the לויים were fined, and a new משנה on when a woman eats תרומה or מעשר through her husband or child.
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא where רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says מעשר ראשון may go to a כהן as well as a לוי, while רבי עקיבא says only a לוי gets it. Each side reads the פסוקים differently. רבי עקיבא points to 'speak to the לויים' and 'eat it in any place.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answers that כהנים are sometimes called לויים, and that 'any place' only means no city wall is needed. A story shows רבי עקיבא blocking רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from a garden by turning its entrance toward a cemetery. אמוראים then explain that the לויים were fined for not going up with עזרא, and argue whether the fined מעשר goes to the poor or to כהנים who are טמא. The גמרא brings the פסוק showing the לויים were missing in עזרא's time, plus רב חסדא's teaching about שוטרים. Finally, a new משנה tracks what a woman may eat, תרומה or מעשר, through her husbands and her living children.

steps.title: The ruling: first tithe goes to a priest
steps.stepSummary: The end of the ברייתא: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says מעשר ראשון is given to a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: [מעשר ראשון is given] to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last word of a ברייתא quoted just before this section. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rules that מעשר ראשון goes to a כהן, against רבי עקיבא, who says it goes to a לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word stands alone and sounds surprising, because the תורה gives מעשר ראשון to the לויים. The גמרא is about to question exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, a descendant of אהרן
A Levite, from the tribe of לוי, who is not a כהן
First tithe: a tenth of the produce, given to the לויים

phrases.english: To a priest.
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's words from the ברייתא just before this: מעשר ראשון goes to a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכֹהֵן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, מעשר ראשון is given to a כהן.

steps.title: Only to a priest and not a Levite?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does he really mean a לוי gets nothing?
steps.simpleTranslation: To a כהן and not to a לוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised. The תורה clearly gives this tithe to the לויים, so how can רבי אלעזר בן עזריה say it goes to a כהן?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, the ruling would cut the לויים out of their own tithe. That cannot be right, so the wording must mean something else.

phrases.english: To a priest and not to a Levite?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכֹהֵן וְלֹא לְלֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the plain meaning of the ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'לכהן' in רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה explicitly gives מעשר ראשון to לויים, so a ruling that gives it only to כהנים contradicts the פסוק.

steps.title: He means 'also to a priest'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה means a כהן may also receive it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say: also to a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading. The לויים still get מעשר ראשון; רבי אלעזר בן עזריה only adds that a כהן may receive it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the argument from 'לוי or כהן' into 'only a לוי, or a לוי and a כהן.' Now the disagreement with רבי עקיבא is clear: רבי עקיבא allows only a לוי.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: מעשר ראשון goes only to a לוי. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: it may go to a לוי or a כהן.

phrases.english: Say: also to a priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא אַף לְכֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gives the tithe only to a כהן and not to a לוי.
steps.terutzMaskana: He means a כהן may also receive it, alongside the לוי.

steps.title: What is רבי עקיבא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי עקיבא limits מעשר ראשון to לויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבי עקיבא's view that only a לוי gets the tithe. This sets up the next step, where the answer comes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the argument is clear, the גמרא wants to see how each side reads the פסוקים. It starts with רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the argument, asks for רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for limiting מעשר ראשון to לויים.

steps.title: The verse speaks to the Levites
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about the tithe says 'speak to the לויים,' so it is only theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And to the לויים you shall speak and say to them.' The פסוק is speaking about לויים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי עקיבא's source. The פסוק about מעשר is addressed to the לויים, so the tithe belongs to them alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the word 'לויים' simply: tribe members who are not כהנים. Since the פסוק names them, a כהן is not included.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And to the Levites you shall speak,
and you shall say to them."
The verse is speaking about Levites.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאֶל הַלְוִיִּם תְּדַבֵּר וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק on מעשר is addressed to the לויים, so only they receive it.

steps.title: Priests are sometimes called Levites
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה follows רבי יהושע בן לוי: in 24 places כהנים are called לויים, so the פסוק can include כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one holds like רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: In twenty-four places כהנים are called לויים, and this is one of them: 'And the כהנים, the לויים, the sons of צדוק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אלעזר בן עזריה deals with רבי עקיבא's פסוק. The word 'לויים' can also mean כהנים, since כהנים are also from the tribe of לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sides argue about one word. For רבי עקיבא, 'לויים' means only non-כהנים. For רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the word can cover כהנים too, as shown by the פסוק in יחזקאל.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other side of the argument)
The sons of צדוק, a family of כהנים

phrases.english: And the other holds like Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
phrases.notes: 'The other' is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the one who said 'also to a כהן.'

phrases.english: as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
In twenty-four places
priests are called Levites,
and this is one of them:
"And the priests, the Levites, the sons of Zadok."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ כִּדְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי אלעזר בן עזריה gets around רבי עקיבא's פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לויים' can include כהנים, so the פסוק allows כהנים to receive מעשר ראשון.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: here it cannot mean priests
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that the tithe must be eaten 'in any place,' and a כהן cannot enter a cemetery, so this פסוק excludes כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא says: Here you cannot say that, since it is written 'You may eat it in any place,' meaning one who can eat it in any place. This excludes a כהן, who cannot eat it in a cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back. Maybe 'לויים' can mean כהנים elsewhere, but not here, because this section of פסוקים says the tithe is eaten 'in any place.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The receiver must be able to eat the tithe anywhere. A כהן may not go into a cemetery, so he cannot eat it everywhere. So the 'לויים' in this section cannot include כהנים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva:
Here you cannot say that,
as it is written: "And you may eat it in any place"
one who can eat it in any place.
This excludes a priest,
who cannot eat it in a cemetery.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הָכָא לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא rejects using רבי יהושע בן לוי's rule for this פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'לויים' in the מעשר section as including כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The tithe goes to someone who can eat it anywhere, and a כהן cannot eat in a cemetery, so this section cannot be speaking about כהנים.

steps.title: 'Any place' means no city wall is needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads 'in any place' as: wherever he wants, with no need for ירושלים's wall, and no lashes for eating it while טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Anywhere he wants, since it does not need the wall. And if he eats it while his body is טמא, he is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's answer. 'In any place' is not about who receives the tithe. It teaches that מעשר ראשון can be eaten anywhere and is less strict than holy foods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Any place' means any city, unlike foods that must be eaten inside ירושלים's walls. The same phrase also teaches that eating it while טמא does not bring lashes. Since the phrase has these meanings, it does not exclude כהנים.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument rests on two readings of 'in any place.' רבי עקיבא: the receiver must be able to eat it anywhere, so not a כהן. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: no city wall is needed, and eating it while טמא brings no lashes.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: How does רבי אלעזר בן עזריה explain 'in any place'?

phrases.english: Anywhere that he wants,
since it does not need the wall,
phrases.notes: Unlike מעשר שני, which has to be eaten inside the walls of ירושלים.

phrases.english: and if he eats it while his body is impure,
he is not lashed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ? כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּבָעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'In any place' describes the receiver, so a כהן is excluded.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'In any place' describes how lenient the tithe is (no wall, no lashes for eating it while טמא), so a כהן is not excluded.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא moves the garden's entrance
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה used to take מעשר ראשון from a garden, so רבי עקיבא moved its entrance to face a cemetery.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain garden from which רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would take מעשר ראשון. רבי עקיבא went and turned its entrance toward the cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story showing the argument in real life. רבי עקיבא blocked the כהן רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from collecting the tithe by making the only entrance face a cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits רבי עקיבא's own reasoning from step 7: a כהן cannot go into a cemetery. With the entrance facing the cemetery, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה could no longer reach the garden.

phrases.english: There was a certain garden

phrases.aramaic: דַּהֲוָה שָׁקֵיל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
phrases.english: from which Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya would take
first tithe.
Rabbi Akiva went
and turned its entrance toward the cemetery.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא גִּינְּתָא דַּהֲוָה שָׁקֵיל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing the two views in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא acted on his view by keeping a כהן from reaching the garden.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's playful complaint
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reacts: 'עקיבא with his bag, and I am supposed to live?'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: עקיבא with his bag, and I am to live?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה responds to what רבי עקיבא did with a sharp, half-joking line. He is complaining that רבי עקיבא cut off the share he felt was his.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line contrasts רבי עקיבא, pictured with his traveler's bag, with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who asks how he is supposed to get by. It is a protest that רבי עקיבא took away what he was entitled to.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was famously wealthy. This is not a real cry of poverty; it is a playful protest about losing what he felt was rightfully his.

phrases.english: He said:
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: Akiva with his satchel, and I am supposed to live?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֲקִיבָא בְּתַרְמִילוֹ, וַאֲנָא חָיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reaction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה protests losing the tithe he believed he was entitled to.

steps.title: Why were the Levites penalized?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic: why did the חכמים penalize the לויים by letting כהנים take מעשר ראשון too?
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: For what reason did they penalize the לויים regarding the tithe? רבי יונתן and the elders argue about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion between אמוראים. It asks why the לויים lost their exclusive right to מעשר ראשון. This step sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This approach treats giving the tithe to כהנים as a rule the חכמים made, called a 'קנס' (penalty). The question is what the reason for it was.

phrases.english: It was stated:
For what reason did they penalize the Levites regarding the tithe?
Rabbi Yonatan and the elders argue about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, מִפְּנֵי מָה קָנְסוּ לְוִיִּם בְּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פסוקים to the reason for the rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the לויים lost their exclusive right to מעשר ראשון.

steps.title: Two reasons: Ezra's time, or helping impure priests
steps.stepSummary: One says it was because the לויים did not come up in the days of עזרא. The other says it was so כהנים could rely on it when they were טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: Because they did not go up in the days of עזרא. And one said: So that the כהנים could rely on it during their days of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the two answers. One is a real penalty for the לויים; the other is a practical help for the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view punishes the לויים for not returning to ארץ ישראל with עזרא. The second explains why כהנים needed it: a טמא כהן may not eat תרומה, but מעשר ראשון may be eaten while טמא, as step 8 showed. So כהנים would always have food.

keyTerms.meaning: עזרא, who led the return from בבל

steps.whatToRemember: At first glance there are two reasons why כהנים may take מעשר ראשון: (1) a penalty on the לויים for not coming up with עזרא; (2) so כהנים have food when they are טמא and cannot eat תרומה. Step 14 recasts this: both views agree on the penalty and argue only about who receives the tithe.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second reason ties back to step 8. Because מעשר ראשון can be eaten while טמא, it can feed a כהן when תרומה is off-limits.

phrases.english: One said:
Because they did not go up in the days of Ezra.
phrases.notes: Meaning they did not move to ארץ ישראל with עזרא when the Jews returned from בבל.

phrases.english: And one said:
So that the priests could rely on it
during their days of impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the two answers to the question in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either a penalty because the לויים did not come up with עזרא, or a way for כהנים to have food while טמא.

steps.title: Why would the לויים be fined for the sake of the כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: The first view (fined for not going up with עזרא) makes sense. But the second view seems strange: why punish the לויים just to help כהנים who are טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says the לויים did not go up. That is why they were fined. But according to the one who says it was so כהנים could rely on it when they are טמא, would they fine the לויים because of the כהנים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the second answer from step 12. A fine only makes sense if the לויים did something wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view gives a reason rooted in the לויים' own behavior: they did not go up. The second view only names a benefit for כהנים, and helping a different group is not a reason to punish the לויים. So the second view seems to lack any reason for a fine.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (sets up a contrast with a view that does not make sense)
In their days of impurity, when כהנים cannot eat תרומה

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says: because they did not go up,
for that reason they fined them.
But according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּסְמְכוּ עָלָיו כֹּהֲנִים בִּימֵי טוּמְאָתָן
phrases.english: it was so that כהנים could rely on it in their days of impurity,
would they fine the לויים because of the כהנים?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ — מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קַנְסִינְהוּ. אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second answer given in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that כהנים got מעשר ראשון so they could rely on it while טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fine needs a wrongdoing by the people being fined. Helping כהנים is not a wrong done by the לויים.

steps.title: Both agree on the fine and argue only about who receives it
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees the לויים were fined for not going up with עזרא. They argue whether the fined מעשר goes to the poor or to כהנים, since כהנים who are טמא count as poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone agrees it was a fine because they did not go up in the days of עזרא. Here they argue about this: one holds the fine is giving it to the poor. The other holds that כהנים in their days of טומאה count as poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reworks the argument. Both sides agree on why the לויים were fined. They disagree only on where the fined מעשר goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the fine is now shared by both views, so the challenge from step 13 disappears. The phrase about כהנים 'relying on it when טמא' was never the reason for the fine. It explains why כהנים may receive it: when they are טמא they cannot eat תרומה, so they are like poor people. The second view therefore gives the fined מעשר to כהנים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the second view gave up on the לויים being fined for not going up. Now both views agree on that. 'So כהנים can rely on it' only explains who receives the מעשר.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees it was a fine
because they did not go up in the days of עזרא.
And here they argue about this:
One master holds: the fine is giving it to the poor,
and the other master holds:
כהנים in their days of impurity count as poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא קְנָסָא שֶׁלֹּא עָלוּ בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by rewriting the argument
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the argument: shared reason, different recipient
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two views gave two different reasons for the fine
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree the fine is for not going up. They argue whether the fined מעשר goes to the poor or to כהנים, who count as poor when טמא.

steps.title: Why did רבי עקיבא move the gate, according to the כהנים view?
steps.stepSummary: If the fined מעשר goes to the poor, רבי עקיבא blocking רבי אלעזר בן עזריה makes sense. But if it goes to כהנים, why stop a כהן from taking it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense according to the one who says the fine goes to the poor. That is why רבי עקיבא turned the entrance toward the cemetery. But according to the one who says it goes to כהנים, why did he turn the entrance toward the cemetery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the two views against the story from step 9, where רבי עקיבא blocked רבי אלעזר בן עזריה from collecting מעשר ראשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מעשר goes to the poor, רבי עקיבא had a reason to stop רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, since he was not poor. But if it goes to כהנים, he was a כהן and should be allowed to take it. So the story seems to fit only the 'poor' view.

keyTerms.meaning: A cemetery (a כהן may not enter it)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says the fine goes to the poor,
for that reason רבי עקיבא turned
the entrance toward the cemetery.
phrases.notes: This is the story from step 9. A כהן can't walk into a cemetery, so the new gate kept רבי אלעזר בן עזריה out.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it goes to כהנים,
why did he turn the entrance toward the cemetery?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר קְנָסָא לַעֲנִיִּים — מִשּׁוּם הָכִי אַהְדְּרֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְפִתְחָא לְבֵי קִבְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the 'to כהנים' view from step 14 against the story in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the fined מעשר goes to כהנים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If כהנים may receive it, a כהן like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה should not have been blocked.

steps.title: A כהן may receive it as a fine, but not claim it as his share
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא's message was: you may get it if it is given to you because of the fine, but you may not come and take it as if it were your own rightful share.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: if you come under the rule of the fine, you may have it. But if you come under the rule of an official share, you may not have it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the story so it fits the 'to כהנים' view as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine lets the owner give מעשר ראשון to a כהן, but it does not make the כהן a full partner who is owed a portion. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה was going in and taking it himself, as if he had a share like a לוי. Moving the gate stopped him from taking it, while he could still accept it if the owner gave it.

keyTerms.meaning: An official share that is owed to you
You have it / you do not have it

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees the לויים were fined for not going up with עזרא. One view gives the fined מעשר to the poor. The other gives it to כהנים, but only as a gift the owner may give, not as a share they can claim.

phrases.english: This is what he meant to him:
phrases.notes: Literally 'this is what he said to him.' רבי עקיבא's action is being explained as a message to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּקָא אָתֵית בְּתוֹרַת קְנָסָא — אִית לָךְ,
phrases.english: if you come under the rule of the fine, you may have it;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי קָא אָתֵית בְּתוֹרַת חֲלוּקָּה — לֵית לָךְ.
phrases.english: but if you come under the rule of an official share, you may not have it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the meaning of an action in a story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Under the view that the fined מעשר goes to כהנים, רבי עקיבא had no reason to block a כהן like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן may receive it because of the fine, but may not take it as his rightful share.

steps.title: How do we know the לויים did not go up with עזרא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the basic fact behind the fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that they did not go up in the days of עזרא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of the fact that both views now rely on. It is setting up the next step, which brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since both views now agree the fine was for not going up, that fact needs a source. This is a request for information, not an attack.

phrases.english: And from where do we know
that they did not go up in the days of עזרא?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא לַן דְּלָא סְלִיקוּ בִּימֵי עֶזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the fact accepted in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing the לויים did not go up with עזרא

steps.title: עזרא found no לויים at the river
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in עזרא says he looked over the people and the כהנים but found no לויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And I gathered them to the river that flows to אהוא, and we camped there three days. I looked over the people and the כהנים, and I found none of the sons of לוי there.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 17 with a פסוק that shows no לויים were among those going up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא checked the group heading to ארץ ישראל. The people and the כהנים were there, but the לויים were missing. That missing group is the basis for the fine.

phrases.english: As it is written:
'And I gathered them to the river that flows to אהוא,
and we camped there three days,
and I looked over the people and the כהנים,
and I found none of the sons of לוי there.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וָאֶקְבְּצֵם אֶל הַנָּהָר הַבָּא עַל אַהֲוָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in עזרא 8:15 says no לויים were found among those going up.

steps.title: רב חסדא: שוטרים came first from לויים, later from ישראלים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that at first שוטרים were chosen only from the לויים, and later only from regular ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: At first they appointed שוטרים only from the לויים, as it says: 'And the שוטרים, the לויים, before you.' Now they appoint שוטרים only from ישראלים, as it says: 'And the שוטרים of the many at your heads.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a related teaching of רב חסדא. It shows another way the לויים lost a role they used to have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows the לויים once served as שוטרים. Later the job passed to 'the many', meaning regular ישראלים. Placed here, it fits the theme of the לויים losing their position after עזרא's time.

keyTerms.meaning: Officers who enforce the rulings of the judges

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
At first they would not appoint officers
except from the לויים,
as it says: 'And the officers, the לויים, before you.'
Now they do not appoint officers
except from ישראלים,
as it says: 'And the officers of the many at your heads.'
phrases.notes: 'The many' is read as the biggest group, regular ישראלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בַּתְּחִלָּה לֹא הָיוּ מֵעֲמִידִים שׁוֹטְרִים אֶלָּא מִן הַלְוִיִּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related teaching about the לויים losing a role
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שוטרים were once appointed only from לויים, and are now appointed only from ישראלים.

steps.title: New משנה: a woman eats תרומה or מעשר through her husband or her child
steps.stepSummary: A בת ישראל married to a כהן eats תרומה, and she still does after he dies if she has his child. Married to a לוי, she eats מעשר, with the same rule about a child. Married to a ישראל, she eats neither, even if she has his child.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בת ישראל who married a כהן may eat תרומה. If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat תרומה. If she married a לוי, she may eat מעשר. If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat מעשר. If she married a ישראל, she may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר. If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It tracks what a woman may eat as she marries a כהן, then a לוי, then a ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her right to eat comes from her current husband, or from a living child of a husband who died. Each new marriage replaces the earlier status: marrying a לוי ends her תרומה, and marrying a ישראל ends her מעשר. A child from a ישראל gives her nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
A woman who is not from a כהן or לוי family
The portion given to כהנים, which only they and their households may eat
Here, מעשר ראשון, given to לויים
And she has a child from him

steps.confusionAlert: Read the משנה as one woman's story in order: first a כהן, then a לוי, then a ישראל. Each new marriage cancels what she could eat before.

phrases.english: משנה:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְכֹהֵן — תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: A בת ישראל who married a כהן may eat תרומה.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת וְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה.
phrases.english: If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat תרומה.
If she married a לוי, she may eat מעשר.

phrases.aramaic: מֵת וְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ בֵּן — תֹּאכַל בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: If he died and she has a son from him, she may eat מעשר.
If she married a ישראל,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֹּאכַל לֹא בִּתְרוּמָה וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: she may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.
If he died and she has a son from him,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֹּאכַל לֹא בִּתְרוּמָה וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: she may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּיסֵּת לְכֹהֵן — תֹּאכַל בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, after the topic of the לויים' fine is finished
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's right to eat תרומה or מעשר follows her current husband, or a child from a husband who died. Marrying a ישראל ends both rights.

steps.title: As each son dies, her right to eat returns or ends
steps.stepSummary: If the son from the ישראל dies, she eats מעשר again because of the לוי's son. If the לוי's son dies, she eats תרומה again because of the כהן's son. If the כהן's son also dies, she eats neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: If her son from the ישראל died, she may eat מעשר. If her son from the לוי died, she may eat תרומה. If her son from the כהן died, she may eat neither תרומה nor מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The text finishes the chain case: the woman has sons from three husbands, and it tells us what she may eat as each son dies, starting with the youngest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that the latest son who is still alive decides her status. When the ישראל's son dies, the לוי's son is now the latest living son, so she gets מעשר. When the לוי's son also dies, the כהן's son is left, so she gets תרומה. When he dies too, no son is left to connect her to a כהן or לוי, so she eats neither.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion given to a כֹּהֵן. Only a כֹּהֵן and his household may eat it.
The tenth of the produce given to a לֵוִי

steps.whatToRemember: Only one son counts at a time: the latest one still alive. When he dies, the son before him takes over, and her right to eat moves with him.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think she gets both תרומה and מעשר while the כהן's son is the latest living son. The text only says she eats תרומה. Her right to מעשר had come only through the לוי's son, and he has died.

phrases.english: If her son from the Israelite died —
she may eat tithe.
If her son from the Levite died —
she may eat terumah.
If her son from the priest died —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תֹּאכַל לֹא בִּתְרוּמָה וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: she may eat neither terumah nor tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת בְּנָהּ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the rules from step 20 and shows what happens as each son dies, starting with the youngest.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her right to eat follows the latest son who is still alive. The ישראל's son's death brings back מעשר, the לוי's son's death brings back תרומה, and the כהן's son's death leaves her with neither.
